questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a lossless dielectric medium having a dielectric constant, $\epsilon_r=9$, has the electric field, $E_x=E_0\sin(kz-2\pi\times10^6 t)$ Vm$^{-1}$ where $E_0$ is the amplitude and $k$ is the wave vector. Among the following options, the incorrect choice is :
options: The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along $+z$
The speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is $10^8$ ms$^{-1}$
The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is $300$ m
The magnetic field is given by the relation $B_y=\dfrac{B_0}{v}\sin(kz-2\pi\times10^6 t)$ where $v$ is the speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium
questions.solution:
From the given equation of the electric field $E_x = E_0 \sin(kz - 2\pi \times 10^6 t)$, the wave is propagating in the $+z$ direction.

The angular frequency is $\omega = 2\pi \times 10^6$ rad/s, which gives the frequency $f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} = 10^6$ Hz.

The speed of the electromagnetic wave in the dielectric medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.

Assuming a non-magnetic medium ($\mu_r = 1$), we get $v = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{9}} = 10^8$ ms$^{-1}$.

The wavelength of the wave inside the medium is $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{10^8}{10^6} = 100$ m.

Option (3) states the wavelength is $300$ m, which is incorrect.

questions.solution:
Given, $\mathrm{B}=3 \times 10^{-8} \cos \left(1.6 \times 10^3 x\right.\left.+48 \times 10^{10} t\right)$
On comparing equations (1) & (2), we get;
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{B}_0 & =3 \times 10^{-8} \\
c & =\frac{\omega}{k}=\frac{48 \times 10^{10}}{1.6 \times 10^3} \\
& =3 \times 10^8
\end{aligned}$
And also, $c=\frac{\mathrm{E}_0}{\mathrm{~B}_0}$
Hence, $E_0=B_0 \times c\begin{aligned}
& =3 \times 10^{-8} \times 3 \times 10^8 \\
& =9
\end{aligned}$
So, the required equation is:
$\mathrm{E}=9 \cos \left(1.6 \times 10^3 x+48 \times 10^{10} t\right)$

\hline & \text { List-I } & & \text { List-II } \\

\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
\(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow\) III According to Gauss's law, total electric flux passing through a closed surface is equal to \(\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\) times the total charge enclosed within the surface. i.e., \(\quad \phi=\oint \mathbf{E}. d \mathbf{A}=\frac{Q}{\varepsilon_0}\)
\(\mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{I}\), According to gauss' law of magnetism, total magnetic flux passing through a bar magnet around its enclosed surface is zero because the magnetic lines of forces emerging from North-pole is equal to magnetic lines of force entering into South direction.
i.e., \(\oint B. d A=0\)
\(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow\) II, The electromotive force in a wire is the line integral,
\(E=\int \mathbf{E} \cdot d \mathbf{l}\)...(i)
But, by Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, (EMI)
\(\varepsilon=-\frac{d \phi B}{d t}\)
From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\(\int \mathbf{E} \cdot d \mathbf{l}=-\frac{d \phi B}{d t}\)
\(\mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{IV}\), According to the Maxwell, when electric field and hence electric flux charges with time, then an additional current comes into existence to the conduction current called displacement current. Therefore, the total current across the loop,
\(I=I_c+I_d\)
Hence, the modified form of the Ampere's law is
\(\oint \mathbf{B} \cdot d \mathbf{l}=\mu_0\left[I_c+I_d\right]\)

questions.q:
Electric field associated with EM wave in free space is given by \(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=30 \sin \left(6 \times 10^8 \mathrm{t}+\mathrm{kz}\right) \hat{\mathrm{i}}\) then match the following columns.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline & \text{Column-I} & & \text{Column-II} \\
\hline \text{(a)} & \text{Direction of propagation of EM wave} & (p) & -y \text{ axis} \\
\hline \text{(b)} & \text{Wave length of EM wave} & (q) & 2 \mathrm{~m}^{-1} \\
\hline \text{(c)} & \text{Direction of magnetic field of EM wave} & (r) & 3.14 m \\
\hline \text{(d)} & \text{Propagation constant 'k' of EM wave} & (s) & '-z' \text{ axis} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
The given electric field of the EM wave is:
\(E=30 \sin \left(6 \times 10^8 t+k z\right) \hat{i}\)
Let's break it down:
a) Direction of propagation: The term \(k z\) in the equation indicates that the wave is propagating in the negative \(z\) -axis (since the sign of \(k z\) is positive in the sine function). Hence, the direction of propagation is along the -z axis.
- b) Wavelength of the EM wave: The propagation constant \(k\) is related to the wavelength by the formula \(k=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\). From column-II, \(k=2, \mathrm{~m}^{-1}\), so the wavelength \(\lambda=\frac{2 \pi}{2}=\pi \approx 3.14, \mathrm{~m}\).
- c) Direction of the magnetic field: Since the electric field is along the \(x\) -axis and the wave is propagating along the \(z\)-axis, the magnetic field must be perpendicular to both and hence lies along the -y axis.
- c) Direction of the magnetic field: Since the electric field is along the \(x\) -axis and the wave is propagating along the \(z\)-axis, the magnetic field must be perpendicular to both and hence lies along the \(-y\) axis.
d) Propagation constant: As discussed, the propagation constant \(k=2, \mathrm{~m}^{-1}\).
Matching the columns:
- a) Direction of propagation \(\rightarrow s\)) -z axis
- b) Wavelength \(\rightarrow\) r) 3.14 m
- c) Direction of the magnetic field \(\rightarrow\) p) -y axis
- d) Propagation constant \(\rightarrow\) q) \(2 \mathrm{~m}-1\)
Thus, the correct answer is:
(2) a-s, b-r, c-p, d-q

\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline & \text{Column-I (Law)} & & \text{Column-II (Mathematical formula)} \\
\hline \text{(A)} & \text{Faraday law} & \text{(P)} & \oint \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}} \cdot \mathrm{d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{q}{\epsilon_0} \\
\hline \text{(B)} & \text{Ampere Maxwell law} & \text{(Q)} & \oint \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}} \cdot \mathrm{d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{A}}=0 \\
\hline \text{(C)} & \text{Gauss law for magnetism} & \text{(R)} & \oint \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{d} \ell}=-\frac{\mathrm{d} \phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
\hline \text{(D)} & \text{Gauss law for electrostatics} & \text{(S)} & \oint \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}} . \mathrm{d} \vec{\ell}=\mu_0 \mathrm{i}+\epsilon_0 \mu_0 \frac{\mathrm{~d} \phi_{\mathrm{E}}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
options: \(A \rightarrow R, B \rightarrow Q, C \rightarrow S, D \rightarrow P\)
\(A \rightarrow P, B \rightarrow S, C \rightarrow Q, D \rightarrow R\)
\(A \rightarrow R, B \rightarrow S, C \rightarrow Q, D \rightarrow P\)

The correct matching of Column-I with Column-II is:
(4) \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}, \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{S}, \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Q}, \mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{P}\)
Here's the breakdown:
- A) Faraday's law: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux. The mathematical expression is:
\(\oint E \cdot d \ell=-\frac{d \phi_B}{d t}\)
So, \(\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}\).
- B) Ampere-Maxwell law: This law is an extension of Ampere's law, which includes the displacement current term. It is expressed as:
\(\oint B \cdot d \ell=\mu_0 I+\mu_0 \varepsilon_0 \frac{d \phi_i}{d t}\)
So, \(B \rightarrow S\).
- C) Gauss's law for magnetism: This law states that the net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero, implying there are no magnetic monopoles. The mathematical expression is:
\(\oint B \cdot d A=1\)
So, \(\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Q}\).
D) Gauss's law for electrostatics: This law relates the electric flux through a closed surface to the charge enclosed by that surface. The mathematical expression is:
\(\oint E \cdot d A=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\)
So, D \(\rightarrow\) P.

questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum has an amplitude of $30\sqrt{2} \text{ V m}^{-1}$. The rms value of the oscillating magnetic field is: (Speed of light in vacuum $= 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$)

Given:
Electric field amplitude, $E_0 = 30\sqrt{2} \text{ V m}^{-1}$
Speed of light, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

First, find the amplitude (peak value) of the magnetic field using the relation $c = \dfrac{E_0}{B_0}$:
$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{2}}{3 \times 10^8} = 10\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-8} \text{ T} = \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

Next, calculate the rms value of the magnetic field using $B_{rms} = \dfrac{B_0}{\sqrt{2}}$:
$B_{rms} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-7}}{\sqrt{2}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

Answer: $1.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a vacuum has a frequency of $3 \times 10^{13}\text{ Hz}$. What is the wavelength of this wave, and to which region of the electromagnetic spectrum does it belong?
questions.solution:
The relationship between the speed of light ($c$), frequency ($ u$), and wavelength ($\lambda$) is given by:
$c = u \lambda$

Given:
Frequency, $ u = 3 imes 10^{13} ext{ Hz}$
Speed of light in vacuum, $c = 3 imes 10^8 ext{ m/s}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for wavelength:
$\lambda = \dfrac{c}{ u}$
$\lambda = \dfrac{3 imes 10^8}{3 imes 10^{13}}$
$\lambda = 10^{-5} ext{ m}$

According to the electromagnetic spectrum, the wavelength range from $10^{-3} ext{ m}$ to $7 imes 10^{-7} ext{ m}$ corresponds to Infrared rays. Therefore, a wavelength of $10^{-5} ext{ m}$ falls in the infrared region.

Multiplying the values instead of dividing leads to the incorrect $9 imes 10^{21} ext{ m}$, and confusing the spectrum ranges leads to incorrectly identifying it as ultraviolet or microwaves.

Answer: $10^{-5} ext{ m}$, Infrared rays

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:

questions.q: A point source of light having a power of $1000\pi \text{ W}$ radiates isotropically in all directions. $t = 1 \text{ minute} = 60 \text{ s}$

Calculating the energy:
$E = 10 \times 10^{-3} \times 60 = 0.6 \text{ J}$

Answer: $0.6 \text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Assertion (A): An electron moving with a constant velocity in a straight line does not produce an electromagnetic wave.
Reason (R): A charge moving with a constant velocity produces both an electric field and a magnetic field in the surrounding space.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is a correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true and Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because an electromagnetic wave is produced only by an accelerating or oscillating charge. An electron moving with a constant velocity has zero acceleration and thus cannot radiate electromagnetic waves.

Reason (R) is also true because a moving charge constitutes a current, which produces a magnetic field, while its intrinsic charge produces an electric field.

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The correct explanation for the Assertion is that the generation of electromagnetic waves requires time-varying electric and magnetic fields that can regenerate each other, which is only possible when the charge is accelerating. Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by:
$\vec{B} = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin(0.5 \times 10^3 x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t) \hat{j}$ T

Which of the following represents the corresponding vector equation for the electric field?
questions.solution:
The phase of the wave is $(kx + \omega t)$. Since both the $x$ term and the $t$ term have the same positive sign, the wave is propagating in the negative $x$-direction ($-\hat{i}$).

The direction of propagation is given by the cross product $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.
We know the magnetic field $\vec{B}$ oscillates along the $+\hat{j}$ direction.
Let the direction of the electric field be $\hat{n}$.
$\hat{n} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}$
Since $\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}$, the electric field must oscillate along the $+\hat{k}$ direction.

The amplitude of the electric field $E_0$ is related to the magnetic field amplitude $B_0$ by:
$E_0 = c B_0 = (3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}) \times (2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}) = 6 \text{ V/m}$

Combining the amplitude, phase, and direction, the electric field equation is:
$\vec{E} = 6 \sin(0.5 \times 10^3 x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t) \hat{k} \text{ V/m}$

Answer: $6 \sin(0.5 \times 10^3 x + 1.5 \times 10^{11} t) \hat{k}$ V/m

questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by $\vec{E} = 30 \sin \left(6\pi \times 10^{10} t - 200\pi x\right) \hat{j} \text{ V/m}$. What is the amplitude of the magnetic field, and to which part of the electromagnetic spectrum does this wave belong?
questions.solution:
Given, $\vec{E} = 30 \sin \left(6\pi \times 10^{10} t - 200\pi x\right) \hat{j} \text{ V/m}$

Comparing with the standard equation $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(\omega t - k x) \hat{j}$, we get:
$E_0 = 30 \text{ V/m}$
$\omega = 6\pi \times 10^{10} \text{ rad/s}$

The amplitude of the magnetic field is:
$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{30}{3 \times 10^8} = 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

The frequency of the electromagnetic wave is:
$f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{6\pi \times 10^{10}}{2\pi} = 3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$

A frequency of $3 \times 10^{10} \text{ Hz}$ falls in the range of Microwaves (which typically span from $10^9 \text{ Hz}$ to $3 \times 10^{11} \text{ Hz}$).

Answer: $10^{-7} \text{ T}$, Microwaves

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two transparent media, $A$ and $B$, have relative permittivities $\epsilon_A$ and $\epsilon_B$, and relative permeabilities $\mu_A$ and $\mu_B$ respectively. The ratio of the speed of light in medium $A$ to that in medium $B$ ($v_A : v_B$) is given by:
questions.solution:
The speed of light $v$ in a material medium is given by the relation:
$v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$
where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, $\mu_r$ is the relative permeability, and $\epsilon_r$ is the relative permittivity of the medium.

For medium $A$, $v_A = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_A \epsilon_A}}$

For medium $B$, $v_B = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_B \epsilon_B}}$

Taking the ratio of the two speeds:
$\dfrac{v_A}{v_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_A \epsilon_A}}}{\dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_B \epsilon_B}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_B \epsilon_B}{\mu_A \epsilon_A}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{\mu_B \epsilon_B}{\mu_A \epsilon_A}}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The speed of light in a transparent material medium is always less than its speed in vacuum.
Reason (R): For any transparent material medium, the product of its relative permittivity and relative permeability is always less than 1.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
The speed of light in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$, where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, $\mu_r$ is the relative permeability, and $\epsilon_r$ is the relative permittivity of the medium.

For any transparent material medium, the relative permittivity (dielectric constant) $\epsilon_r \gt 1$ and relative permeability $\mu_r \approx 1$ (for non-magnetic materials) or slightly different, making their product $\mu_r \epsilon_r \gt 1$.

Since the denominator is greater than 1, the speed of light in the medium $v$ is always less than $c$. Thus, the Assertion is true.

The Reason states that the product is less than 1, which is physically incorrect for transparent media. Therefore, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
If the total average energy density of an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum is $U$, then the amplitude of the oscillating magnetic field is:
(where $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space)
questions.solution:
The total average energy density $U$ of an electromagnetic wave is the sum of the average electric energy density ($u_E$) and the average magnetic energy density ($u_B$).

Since $u_E = u_B$, the total average energy density is $U = 2u_B$.

The average energy density of the magnetic field is given by $u_B = \dfrac{B_{rms}^2}{2\mu_0}$.

Since $B_{rms} = \dfrac{B_0}{\sqrt{2}}$, we have $u_B = \dfrac{B_0^2}{4\mu_0}$.

Therefore, the total average energy density is:
$U = 2 \times \left(\dfrac{B_0^2}{4\mu_0}\right) = \dfrac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}$

Rearranging for the amplitude of the magnetic field $B_0$ gives:
$B_0^2 = 2\mu_0 U \implies B_0 = \sqrt{2\mu_0 U}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2\mu_0 U}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For a charging circular parallel plate capacitor, the induced magnetic field at the central axis connecting the plates is zero.

Reason (R): The displacement current density is zero at the central axis of the capacitor.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: According to the Ampere-Maxwell law, $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{d,\text{enclosed}}$. At the central axis ($r = 0$), an Amperian loop encloses zero area, meaning the enclosed displacement current is zero. Hence, the induced magnetic field $B$ is zero.

Reason (R) is incorrect: The changing electric field $E$ is uniform across the entire area of the plates. Therefore, the displacement current density $J_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{dE}{dt}$ is uniform and non-zero everywhere between the plates, including at the central axis.

Thus, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR), wavelength increases from violet to red. Therefore, the wavelength of red light is indeed greater than that of blue light. Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.

In a vacuum, all electromagnetic waves (including red and blue light) travel at the same constant speed, $c = 3 \times 10^{8}\text{ m/s}$. The speed of light in vacuum is independent of its wavelength. Hence, Reason (R) is incorrect.

Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular parallel plate capacitor of radius $R$ is being charged such that the electric field between the plates changes at a uniform rate. Which of the following correctly describes the variation of the induced magnetic field $B$ with the radial distance $r$ from the central axis of the plates?
options: $B$ increases linearly with $r$ for $r \lt  R$, and decreases as $1/r$ for $r \gt  R$.
$B$ is constant for $r \lt  R$, and is zero for $r \gt  R$.
$B$ is zero for $r \lt  R$, and decreases as $1/r$ for $r \gt  R$.
$B$ increases as $r^2$ for $r \lt  R$, and decreases as $1/r^2$ for $r \gt  R$.
questions.solution:
According to the Ampere-Maxwell law, the line integral of the magnetic field along a circular Amperian loop of radius $r$ is $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{d,\text{enclosed}}$.

For a point inside the capacitor ($r \lt R$), the enclosed displacement current is proportional to the area: $I_{d,\text{enclosed}} = I_d \left(\dfrac{\pi r^2}{\pi R^2}\right)$.
Therefore, $B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 I_d \dfrac{r^2}{R^2} \Rightarrow B = \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{2\pi R^2}\right) r$.
This shows that $B$ increases linearly with $r$ for $r \lt R$.

For a point outside the capacitor ($r \gt R$), the enclosed displacement current is the total displacement current $I_d$.
Therefore, $B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 I_d \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{2\pi r}$.
This shows that $B$ decreases as $1/r$ for $r \gt R$.

Hence, the magnetic field increases linearly with $r$ inside the plates and decreases as $1/r$ outside the plates.

Answer: $B$ increases linearly with $r$ for $r \lt R$, and decreases as $1/r$ for $r \gt R$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is travelling in a lossless, non-magnetic dielectric medium having a dielectric constant $\epsilon_r = 2.25$. If the wave is propagating along the $-y$ direction and the electric field oscillates along the $+z$ axis, which of the following is the correct vector equation for the magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The speed of the electromagnetic wave in the dielectric medium is $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_r}} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{2.25}} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5} = 2 \times 10^8$ m/s.

The amplitude of the magnetic field is $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{v} = \dfrac{60}{2 \times 10^8} = 3 \times 10^{-7}$ T.

The wave vector is $k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ rad/m.

The angular frequency is $\omega = kv = \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \times (2 \times 10^8) = \pi \times 10^8$ rad/s.

Since the wave propagates in the $-y$ direction, the phase argument must be of the form $(ky + \omega t)$.

The direction of propagation is given by the direction of $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.
Given $\hat{E} = \hat{k}$ and $\hat{v} = -\hat{j}$, we have $\hat{k} \times \hat{B} = -\hat{j}$.
Since $\hat{k} \times \hat{i} = \hat{j}$, it follows that $\hat{B} = -\hat{i}$.

Therefore, the complete vector equation for the magnetic field is:
$\vec{B} = -3 \times 10^{-7} \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} y + \pi \times 10^8 t\right) \hat{i}$ T.

Answer: $\vec{B} = -3 \times 10^{-7} \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} y + \pi \times 10^8 t\right) \hat{i}$ T

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is propagating along the positive $z$-axis. If the electric field vector is oscillating parallel to the vector $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$, which of the following represents a possible direction for the magnetic field vector?
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

Given that the wave propagates along the positive $z$-axis ($+\hat{k}$) and the electric field $\vec{E}$ is parallel to $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$.

Let us check the cross product for the given options:

For option 1: $(\hat{i} + \hat{j}) \times (-\hat{i} + \hat{j}) = (\hat{i} \times -\hat{i}) + (\hat{i} \times \hat{j}) + (\hat{j} \times -\hat{i}) + (\hat{j} \times \hat{j}) = 0 + \hat{k} - (-\hat{k}) + 0 = 2\hat{k}$. This points in the $+z$ direction, which matches the given propagation direction.

For option 2: $(\hat{i} + \hat{j}) \times (\hat{i} - \hat{j}) = -\hat{k} - \hat{k} = -2\hat{k}$ (points in $-z$ direction).

For options 3 and 4: The cross product with $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$ yields zero, meaning they are parallel or anti-parallel, which violates the condition that $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ are perpendicular.

Thus, the magnetic field must be parallel to $(-\hat{i} + \hat{j})$.

Answer: $-\hat{i} + \hat{j}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The ratio of the amplitude of the electric field to the magnetic field ($E_0/B_0$) decreases when a plane electromagnetic wave enters a non-magnetic dielectric medium from vacuum.
Reason (R): The speed of the electromagnetic wave decreases in the dielectric medium, and the ratio $E_0/B_0$ is equal to the speed of the wave.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
The ratio of the amplitude of the electric field ($E_0$) to the magnetic field ($B_0$) in any medium is equal to the speed of the electromagnetic wave ($v$) in that medium, i.e., $\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = v$.

When an electromagnetic wave enters a dielectric medium from vacuum, its speed decreases from $c$ to $v = \dfrac{c}{n}$, where $n \gt 1$ is the refractive index of the medium.

Since the speed $v$ decreases, the ratio $\dfrac{E_0}{B_0}$ also decreases.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave travelling in a transparent medium is given by:
$B_y = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ T}$
The corresponding expression for the electric field vector is:
questions.solution:
From the given magnetic field equation, $B_y = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ T}$, we can extract:
Wave number, $k = 10^3 \text{ rad/m}$
Angular frequency, $\omega = 2 \times 10^{11} \text{ rad/s}$
Magnetic field amplitude, $B_0 = 2 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}$

The speed of the wave in the medium is:
$v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{11}}{10^3} = 2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

The amplitude of the electric field is:
$E_0 = v B_0 = (2 \times 10^8) \times (2 \times 10^{-8}) = 4 \text{ V/m}$

The phase argument $(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t)$ indicates that the wave propagates in the $+z$ direction ($\hat{v} = \hat{k}$).
The magnetic field is in the $+y$ direction ($\hat{B} = \hat{j}$).
The direction of propagation is given by the cross product $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v}$.
We need $\hat{E} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$.
Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, the electric field must oscillate in the $+x$ direction ($\hat{i}$).

Therefore, the electric field vector is:
$E_x = 4 \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ V/m}$

Answer: $E_x = 4 \sin\left(10^3 z - 2 \times 10^{11} t\right) \text{ V/m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following represents the typical wavelength range of the electromagnetic wave that is widely used for studying crystal structures?
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic waves used for studying crystal structures are X-rays.

According to the electromagnetic spectrum, X-rays have a typical wavelength range from about $10^{-8}\text{ m}$ (10 nm) down to $10^{-13}\text{ m}$ ($10^{-4}$ nm).

The range $4 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$ to $6 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$ corresponds to ultraviolet rays.

The range $10^{-3}\text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$ corresponds to infrared waves.

The range $0.3\text{ m}$ to $10^{-3}\text{ m}$ corresponds to microwaves.

Answer: $10^{-8}\text{ m}$ to $10^{-13}\text{ m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field inside a circular parallel plate capacitor of radius $R$ is observed to be directly proportional to the radial distance $r$ from the central axis. If the magnitude of this magnetic field at any fixed point inside the capacitor is constant in time, what is the time dependence of the electric field $E$ between the plates?
questions.solution:
According to the Ampere-Maxwell law, the magnetic field $B$ inside the capacitor at a radial distance $r$ is given by $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I_{d,\text{enclosed}}$.

Since the enclosed displacement current $I_{d,\text{enclosed}} = J_d (\pi r^2)$, we have $B(2\pi r) = \mu_0 J_d \pi r^2 \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{\mu_0 J_d r}{2}$.

We are given that $B$ is constant in time at any fixed point $r$. This implies that the displacement current density $J_d$ must be constant in time.

The displacement current density is related to the electric field by $J_d = \epsilon_0 \dfrac{dE}{dt}$.

For $J_d$ to be a non-zero constant, the rate of change of the electric field $\dfrac{dE}{dt}$ must be constant. Therefore, the electric field $E$ must vary linearly with time.

Answer: $E$ varies linearly with time

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a vacuum, the speed of ultraviolet rays is equal to the speed of infrared rays.

Reason (R): Ultraviolet rays have a higher frequency than infrared rays.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
In a vacuum, all electromagnetic waves travel with the same speed, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$, regardless of their wavelength or frequency. Therefore, the speed of ultraviolet rays is equal to the speed of infrared rays. Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.

In the electromagnetic spectrum, the frequency increases in the order: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays. Thus, ultraviolet rays have a higher frequency than infrared rays. Hence, Reason (R) is correct.

However, the higher frequency of ultraviolet rays is not the reason they travel at the same speed as infrared rays. The constant speed of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum is determined by the electric permittivity and magnetic permeability of free space. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating in a vacuum is given by the equation:
$\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t) \hat{i}$

Which of the following describes the state of motion of the source charge that could have produced this wave?
options: Moving with a uniform velocity along the z-axis
Oscillating along the y-axis with a frequency of $\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}$
Oscillating along the x-axis with a frequency of $\omega$
Oscillating along the x-axis with a frequency of $\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}$
questions.solution:
An electromagnetic wave is produced by an accelerating or oscillating charge, not by a charge moving with uniform velocity. Thus, the source charge must be oscillating.

The given electric field equation $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t) \hat{i}$ indicates that the wave propagates along the z-axis and the electric field oscillates along the x-axis (due to the $\hat{i}$ direction).

Since the electric field of the radiated wave is parallel to the direction of acceleration of the source charge, the charge must be oscillating along the x-axis.

The angular frequency of the wave is $\omega$. The linear frequency of the wave, and hence the frequency of the oscillating source charge, is $f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}$.

Answer: Oscillating along the x-axis with a frequency of $\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Microwaves are often referred to as heat waves.

Reason (R): Water molecules present in most materials readily absorb infrared waves, increasing their thermal motion and heating the surroundings.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Infrared waves are often referred to as heat waves, not microwaves. Therefore, the Assertion (A) is false.

The Reason (R) is a true statement according to NCERT. Water molecules (along with other molecules like $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{NH}_3$) present in most materials readily absorb infrared waves. After absorption, their thermal motion increases, which causes them to heat up and heat their surroundings.

Since (A) is false and (R) is true, the correct option is the fourth one.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is found to have a wavelength of the order of $1\text{ \AA}$ ($10^{-10}\text{ m}$). Identify the electromagnetic wave and the standard method used to produce it.
options: X-rays; produced by bombarding a metal target with high energy electrons.
Gamma rays; produced by the radioactive decay of the nucleus.
Ultraviolet rays; produced by special lamps and very hot bodies.
X-rays; produced by the vibration of atoms and molecules.
questions.solution:
The wavelength of $1\text{ \AA}$ ($10^{-10}\text{ m}$) falls in the characteristic range of X-rays, which typically span from $10^{-8}\text{ m}$ to $10^{-13}\text{ m}$.

According to the electromagnetic spectrum, X-rays are commonly produced by bombarding a metal target with high energy electrons.

Gamma rays generally have even shorter wavelengths and are of nuclear origin. Ultraviolet rays have longer wavelengths ($10^{-8}\text{ m}$ to $4 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$). The vibration of atoms and molecules produces infrared waves, not X-rays.

Answer: X-rays; produced by bombarding a metal target with high energy electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in a transparent non-magnetic medium is given by $\vec{E} = 40 \sin(1.2 \times 10^8 t - 0.6 z) \hat{i} \text{ V/m}$. The corresponding magnetic field equation will be:
questions.solution:
Given the electric field equation: $\vec{E} = 40 \sin(1.2 \times 10^8 t - 0.6 z) \hat{i} \text{ V/m}$
Comparing with the standard equation $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(\omega t - kz) \hat{i}$, we get:
$E_0 = 40 \text{ V/m}$
$\omega = 1.2 \times 10^8 \text{ rad/s}$
$k = 0.6 \text{ rad/m}$

The speed of the wave in the medium is:
$v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{1.2 \times 10^8}{0.6} = 2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

The amplitude of the magnetic field is:
$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{v} = \dfrac{40}{2 \times 10^8} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

The wave propagates in the $+z$ direction (since the phase is $\omega t - kz$), so $\hat{v} = \hat{k}$.
The direction of the magnetic field is given by $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v}$.
$\hat{i} \times \hat{B} = \hat{k} \Rightarrow \hat{B} = \hat{j}$

Therefore, the magnetic field equation is:
$\vec{B} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \sin(1.2 \times 10^8 t - 0.6 z) \hat{j} \text{ T}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-7} \sin(1.2 \times 10^8 t - 0.6 z) \hat{j} \text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic spectrum ordered by increasing frequency (or decreasing wavelength) is: Radio waves < Microwaves < Infrared rays < Visible light < Ultraviolet rays < X-rays < Gamma rays.

Among the given options, X-rays are located nearest to the high-frequency end of the spectrum, meaning they have the highest frequency.

Answer: X-rays

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by $\vec{E} = 60 \sin \left(1.5 \times 10^7 t - 0.05 z\right) \hat{i} \text{ V/m}$. The corresponding magnetic field vector equation will be:
questions.solution:
Given, $\vec{E} = 60 \sin \left(1.5 \times 10^7 t - 0.05 z\right) \hat{i} \text{ V/m}$

Comparing with the standard equation $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(\omega t - k z) \hat{i}$, we get:
$E_0 = 60 \text{ V/m}$
$\omega = 1.5 \times 10^7 \text{ rad/s}$
$k = 0.05 \text{ rad/m}$

The speed of the wave is $c = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{1.5 \times 10^7}{0.05} = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$.
The amplitude of the magnetic field is $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c} = \dfrac{60}{3 \times 10^8} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$.

The argument $(\omega t - k z)$ indicates that the wave is propagating in the $+z$ direction, so the unit vector of propagation is $\hat{k}$.
The direction of propagation is given by $\hat{E} \times \hat{B}$.
$\hat{i} \times \hat{B} = \hat{k}$
Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, the magnetic field must oscillate in the $+\hat{j}$ direction.

Therefore, the magnetic field equation is:
$\vec{B} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \sin \left(1.5 \times 10^7 t - 0.05 z\right) \hat{j} \text{ T}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-7} \sin \left(1.5 \times 10^7 t - 0.05 z\right) \hat{j} \text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For an electromagnetic wave propagating in a non-magnetic medium with relative permittivity $\epsilon_r = 4$, if the electric field amplitude is $E_0$, the corresponding magnetic field amplitude is $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{2c}$ (where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum).

Reason (R): The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$, and the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $E_0 = v B_0$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
The speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.
For a non-magnetic medium, the relative permeability $\mu_r = 1$. Given $\epsilon_r = 4$, the speed of the wave is $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{1 \times 4}} = \dfrac{c}{2}$.

The amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $E_0 = v B_0$.
Substituting the value of $v$, we get $E_0 = \left(\dfrac{c}{2}\right) B_0$, which gives $B_0 = \dfrac{2E_0}{c}$.

The Assertion incorrectly states that $B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{2c}$. The Reason correctly states the standard formulas for wave speed and the amplitude relation. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum has a magnetic field amplitude of $3.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}$ and a wavelength of $600 \text{ nm}$. The amplitude of the oscillating electric field is: (Speed of light in vacuum $= 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
Given:
Magnetic field amplitude, $B_0 = 3.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T}$
Speed of light, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

The ratio of the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields in vacuum is equal to the speed of light, independent of the wavelength.

Using the relation $c = \dfrac{E_0}{B_0}$, we get:
$E_0 = c \times B_0$
$E_0 = (3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}) \times (3.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T})$
$E_0 = 9.0 \text{ V m}^{-1}$

The wavelength data ($600 \text{ nm}$) is extraneous information and is not required for this calculation.

Answer: $9.0 \text{ V m}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The momentum transferred to a completely absorbing surface of area $A$ exposed to normally incident light of intensity $I$ for time $t$ is $\dfrac{IAt}{c}$.

Reason (R): The total energy incident on the surface is $IAt$ and the momentum transferred by the absorbed electromagnetic wave is its energy divided by the speed of light $c$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Intensity $I$ is defined as the energy incident per unit area per unit time. Therefore, the total energy $E$ incident on a surface of area $A$ in time $t$ is given by $E = IAt$.

For a completely absorbing surface, the entire incident energy is absorbed. The momentum $p$ transferred by an electromagnetic wave is related to its energy $E$ by the relation $p = \dfrac{E}{c}$, where $c$ is the speed of light.

Substituting the expression for energy, we get $p = \dfrac{IAt}{c}$.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) provides the correct logical derivation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct decreasing order of wavelengths for the given electromagnetic waves?
options: Microwaves > Red light > Blue light > X-rays
X-rays > Blue light > Red light > Microwaves
Microwaves > Blue light > Red light > X-rays
Red light > Microwaves > X-rays > Blue light
questions.solution:
The complete electromagnetic spectrum in decreasing order of wavelength is: Radio waves > Microwaves > Infrared > Visible light > Ultraviolet > X-rays > Gamma rays.

Within the visible spectrum, wavelength decreases from red to violet (VIBGYOR). Therefore, red light has a longer wavelength than blue light.

Combining both sequences, the correct decreasing order of wavelengths is: Microwaves > Red light > Blue light > X-rays.

Answer: Microwaves > Red light > Blue light > X-rays

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Wave Equation)List II (Direction of complementary field)
(A) $\vec{E} = E_0 \sin(kz - \omega t) \hat{i}$(I) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{k}$
(B) $\vec{B} = B_0 \cos(\omega t + ky) \hat{i}$(II) $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{i}$
(C) $\vec{E} = E_0 \cos(kx - \omega t) \hat{j}$(III) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$
(D) $\vec{B} = B_0 \sin(kz + \omega t) \hat{j}$(IV) $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{k}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of the cross product $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

(A) $\vec{E}$ is along $\hat{i}$ and the wave propagates along $+z$ direction ($\hat{k}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{i} \times \hat{B} = \hat{k}$. Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$ (Matches III).

(B) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{i}$ and the wave propagates along $-y$ direction ($-\hat{j}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{E} \times \hat{i} = -\hat{j}$. Since $(-\hat{k}) \times \hat{i} = -\hat{j}$, $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{k}$ (Matches IV).

(C) $\vec{E}$ is along $\hat{j}$ and the wave propagates along $+x$ direction ($\hat{i}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{j} \times \hat{B} = \hat{i}$. Since $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$, $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{k}$ (Matches I).

(D) $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$ and the wave propagates along $-z$ direction ($-\hat{k}$).
$\hat{E} \times \hat{B} = \hat{v} \Rightarrow \hat{E} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{k}$. Since $(-\hat{i}) \times \hat{j} = -\hat{k}$, $\vec{E}$ is along $-\hat{i}$ (Matches II).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider the following three electromagnetic waves: Microwaves ($M$), Infrared rays ($I$), and Ultraviolet rays ($U$). Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their photon energies?
questions.solution:
The energy of a photon is given by $E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength.

The order of wavelengths for the given electromagnetic waves is:
$\lambda_{Ultraviolet} \lt \lambda_{Infrared} \lt \lambda_{Microwaves}$

Since photon energy is inversely proportional to wavelength, the order of their energies is:
$E_{Microwaves} \lt E_{Infrared} \lt E_{Ultraviolet}$

Thus, the correct increasing order is $E_M \lt E_I \lt E_U$.

Answer: $E_M \lt E_I \lt E_U$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the production of electromagnetic waves is incorrect?
options: X-rays are produced by bombarding a metal target with high-speed electrons.
Radio waves are produced by the accelerated motion of charges in conducting wires.
Microwaves are produced by the vibration of atoms and molecules in hot bodies.
Gamma rays are produced during the radioactive decay of atomic nuclei.
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is correct because X-rays are produced by the sudden deceleration of high-speed electrons when they strike a heavy metal target.

Statement 2 is correct because radio waves are generated by the accelerated or oscillating motion of charges in conducting wires.

Statement 4 is correct because gamma rays are of nuclear origin, produced during the radioactive decay of unstable nuclei.

Statement 3 is incorrect because microwaves are produced by special vacuum tubes such as klystron valves, magnetron valves, and Gunn diodes. It is infrared waves that are produced by hot bodies and the vibration of atoms and molecules.

Answer: Microwaves are produced by the vibration of atoms and molecules in hot bodies.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transparent, non-magnetic medium has a dielectric constant of $2.25$. What is the speed of light in this medium? (Take the speed of light in vacuum as $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$)
questions.solution:
For a non-magnetic medium, the relative permeability is approximately unity ($\mu_r = 1$).

The speed of light in a material medium is given by the relation:
$v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$

Substituting the given values ($\epsilon_r = 2.25$, $\mu_r = 1$, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$):
$v = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{1 \times 2.25}}$

$v = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5} = 2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-IList-II
(A) A point charge at rest(I) Produces both electric and magnetic fields but no electromagnetic waves
(B) A point charge moving with constant velocity(II) Produces only an electric field
(C) A steady current in a neutral straight wire(III) Produces electromagnetic waves
(D) An oscillating point charge(IV) Produces only a magnetic field

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
A point charge at rest produces only an electrostatic field in the surrounding space.

A point charge moving with a constant velocity produces both electric and magnetic fields, but these fields do not vary with time in a way that generates electromagnetic waves.

A steady current in a neutral straight wire produces only a magnetic field around it, as the net charge is zero.

An oscillating point charge is an accelerated charge, which produces time-varying electric and magnetic fields that propagate through space as electromagnetic waves.

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Three electromagnetic waves $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ are identified by their production mechanisms as follows:
$X$ : Produced during the radioactive decay of a nucleus
$Y$ : Produced by the vibration of atoms and molecules
$Z$ : Produced by a magnetron valve

Which of the following represents the correct increasing order of their wavelengths in vacuum?
questions.solution:
Wave $X$ is produced by the radioactive decay of a nucleus, which identifies it as a gamma ray.

Wave $Y$ is produced by the vibration of atoms and molecules, which identifies it as an infrared ray.

Wave $Z$ is produced by a magnetron valve, which identifies it as a microwave.

The electromagnetic spectrum, in order of increasing wavelength, is: gamma rays < X-rays < ultraviolet < visible < infrared < microwaves < radio waves.

Therefore, the increasing order of their wavelengths is $X \lt Y \lt Z$.

Answer: $X \lt Y \lt Z$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum, the average energy density of the electric field is equal to the average energy density of the magnetic field.
Reason (R): In vacuum, the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $E_0 = cB_0$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The average energy density of the electric field is $u_E = \dfrac{1}{4}\epsilon_0 E_0^2$.

The average energy density of the magnetic field is $u_B = \dfrac{B_0^2}{4\mu_0}$.

In vacuum, the speed of light is $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}}$, and the field amplitudes are related by $E_0 = cB_0$.

Substituting $E_0$ into the expression for $u_E$:
$u_E = \dfrac{1}{4}\epsilon_0 (cB_0)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}\epsilon_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{\mu_0\epsilon_0}\right) B_0^2 = \dfrac{B_0^2}{4\mu_0} = u_B$.

Thus, the average energy densities are equal, making the Assertion (A) correct. The Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact mathematical relationship required to prove the Assertion. Therefore, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An LC circuit is used as a transmitter to generate electromagnetic waves in free space. If the circuit contains an inductor of inductance $L = \dfrac{2.5}{\pi^2}$ mH and a capacitor of capacitance $C = 1\mu$F, what is the wavelength of the emitted electromagnetic wave?
(Take the speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times 10^8$ m/s)
questions.solution:
The frequency of the emitted electromagnetic wave is equal to the resonant frequency of the oscillating charge in the LC circuit.

The resonant frequency is given by:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \sqrt{LC}}$

Given $L = \dfrac{2.5}{\pi^2} \times 10^{-3}$ H and $C = 10^{-6}$ F, we have:
$LC = \dfrac{2.5 \times 10^{-9}}{\pi^2} = \dfrac{25 \times 10^{-10}}{\pi^2}$

$\sqrt{LC} = \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi}$ s

Substituting this into the frequency formula:
$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \left( \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-5}}{\pi} \right)} = \dfrac{1}{10 \times 10^{-5}} = 10^4$ Hz

The wavelength $\lambda$ of the electromagnetic wave in free space is:
$\lambda = \dfrac{c}{f} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{10^4} = 3 \times 10^4$ m

Answer: $3 \times 10^4$ m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solar panel of area $10 \text{ cm}^2$ is exposed to sunlight having an average intensity of $50 \text{ W cm}^{-2}$. If the total energy received by the panel is $3 \times 10^5 \text{ J}$, what is the duration of this exposure in minutes?
questions.solution:
The total energy $E$ received by a surface is given by the product of intensity $I$, area $A$, and time $t$:

$E = I \times A \times t$

Given:
$I = 50 \text{ W cm}^{-2}$
$A = 10 \text{ cm}^2$
$E = 3 \times 10^5 \text{ J}$

First, calculate the total power received by the panel:
$P = I \times A = 50 \text{ W cm}^{-2} \times 10 \text{ cm}^2 = 500 \text{ W}$

Now, substitute the power into the energy equation to find the time in seconds:
$t = \dfrac{E}{P} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^5 \text{ J}}{500 \text{ W}} = 600 \text{ s}$

Finally, convert the time from seconds to minutes:
$t = \dfrac{600}{60} \text{ minutes} = 10 \text{ minutes}$

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of total intensity $I$ is propagating in vacuum. If $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, the average energy density of the magnetic field component of this wave is:
questions.solution:
The total intensity $I$ of an electromagnetic wave is related to its total average energy density $u$ by the equation:

$I = u c$

$\Rightarrow u = \dfrac{I}{c}$

In an electromagnetic wave, the total energy is shared equally between the electric and magnetic fields. Thus, the average energy density of the magnetic field ($u_B$) is exactly half of the total average energy density.

$u_B = \dfrac{u}{2} = \dfrac{I}{2c}$

Answer: $\dfrac{I}{2c}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by:
$\vec{B} = B_0 \cos(ky + \omega t) \hat{i}$

Consider the following statements regarding this wave:
(A) The wave propagates in the negative y-direction.
(B) The corresponding electric field oscillates along the negative z-direction.
(C) The amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields are related by $E_0 = \dfrac{B_0}{c}$.
(D) The electric and magnetic fields oscillate in phase with each other.

Choose the correct combination of statements from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The argument of the cosine function is $(ky + \omega t)$, which indicates that the wave propagates in the negative y-direction. Thus, statement (A) is correct.

The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of $\hat{E} \times \hat{B}$. Here, the propagation direction is $-\hat{j}$ and the magnetic field is along $\hat{i}$.
Let the electric field direction be $\hat{E}$. We require $\hat{E} \times \hat{i} = -\hat{j}$.
Since $(-\hat{k}) \times \hat{i} = -\hat{j}$, the electric field oscillates along the negative z-direction. Thus, statement (B) is correct.

The amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields in vacuum are related by $E_0 = c B_0$. Statement (C) is incorrect.

In a plane electromagnetic wave, the electric and magnetic fields oscillate in phase. Thus, statement (D) is correct.

Therefore, the correct combination is (A), (B) and (D).

Answer: (A), (B) and (D) only

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

(A)$\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$(I)$+x$-direction
(B)$\vec{E}$ along $-\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$(II)$-x$-direction
(C)$\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{k}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{i}$(III)$+y$-direction
(D)$\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{i}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{k}$(IV)$-y$-direction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of the vector $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

(A) $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$: Direction is $\hat{j} \times \hat{k} = \hat{i}$ ($+x$-direction). Matches with (I).

(B) $\vec{E}$ along $-\hat{j}$, $\vec{B}$ along $+\hat{k}$: Direction is $(-\hat{j}) \times \hat{k} = -\hat{i}$ ($-x$-direction). Matches with (II).

(C) $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{k}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{i}$: Direction is $\hat{k} \times (-\hat{i}) = -\hat{j}$ ($-y$-direction). Matches with (IV).

(D) $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{i}$, $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{k}$: Direction is $\hat{i} \times (-\hat{k}) = \hat{j}$ ($+y$-direction). Matches with (III).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the typical wavelength ranges of electromagnetic waves.

List-IList-II
(A) AM Radio waves(I) $\gt 0.1 \text{ m}$
(B) Microwaves(II) $0.1 \text{ m to } 10^{-3} \text{ m}$
(C) X-rays(III) $10^{-9} \text{ m to } 10^{-12} \text{ m}$
(D) Gamma rays(IV) $\lt 10^{-12} \text{ m}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the standard electromagnetic spectrum:
AM Radio waves have the longest wavelengths, typically $\gt 0.1 \text{ m}$.
Microwaves fall in the range of $0.1 \text{ m}$ to $1 \text{ mm}$ ($10^{-3} \text{ m}$).
X-rays have much shorter wavelengths, ranging from $1 \text{ nm}$ ($10^{-9} \text{ m}$) to $10^{-3} \text{ nm}$ ($10^{-12} \text{ m}$).
Gamma rays have the shortest wavelengths, typically $\lt 10^{-3} \text{ nm}$ ($\lt 10^{-12} \text{ m}$).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Assertion (A): In a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum, the ratio of the instantaneous magnitudes of the electric and magnetic fields ($E/B$) is always constant and equal to $c$.

Reason (R): In an electromagnetic wave, the electric and magnetic fields oscillate in phase and the ratio of their amplitudes is $c$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
The instantaneous electric and magnetic fields in a plane electromagnetic wave are given by:

$E = E_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)$
$B = B_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)$

Since the fields oscillate in phase, the sine terms are identical. The ratio of their instantaneous magnitudes is:

$\dfrac{E}{B} = \dfrac{E_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)}{B_0 \sin(kx - \omega t)} = \dfrac{E_0}{B_0}$

Since the ratio of their amplitudes $\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = c$, the instantaneous ratio $\dfrac{E}{B}$ is also constant and equal to $c$.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular parallel plate capacitor of radius $R$ is being charged, establishing a uniform displacement current $I_d$ between its plates. What is the ratio of the magnitude of the induced magnetic field at a radial distance $r = R/2$ to that at a radial distance $r = 2R$ from the central axis of the capacitor?
questions.solution:
Let the total displacement current be $I_d$.

For a point inside the region between the capacitor plates ($r \lt R$), the magnetic field is given by Ampere-Maxwell's law:
$B_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d r}{2\pi R^2}$
At $r = R/2$:
$B(R/2) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d (R/2)}{2\pi R^2} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{4\pi R}$

For a point outside the region between the plates ($r \gt R$), the magnetic field is:
$B_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{2\pi r}$
At $r = 2R$:
$B(2R) = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{2\pi (2R)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{4\pi R}$

The ratio of the magnetic fields is:
$\dfrac{B(R/2)}{B(2R)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{4\pi R}}{\dfrac{\mu_0 I_d}{4\pi R}} = 1$

Thus, the required ratio is $1:1$.

Answer: $1:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The spatial variation of the electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum at a given instant is described by a sinusoidal curve. The curve has a peak value of $60 \text{ V m}^{-1}$ and a spatial period of $0.5 \text{ m}$. The amplitude of the oscillating magnetic field is: (Speed of light in vacuum = $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
From the given description of the spatial variation, the peak value of the electric field is its amplitude, $E_0 = 60 \text{ V m}^{-1}$.

The spatial period (wavelength) is extra information and is not required to find the magnetic field amplitude.

Using the relation between the amplitudes of the electric and magnetic fields in vacuum:

$B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{c}$

$B_0 = \dfrac{60}{3 \times 10^8} = 20 \times 10^{-8} \text{ T} = 2.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

Answer: $2.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Infrared waves are often referred to as heat waves.
Reason (R): They are produced by the vibration of atoms and molecules, and their absorption by water molecules in materials increases thermal motion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Infrared waves are produced by hot bodies and molecules due to the vibration of atoms and molecules.

They are commonly known as heat waves because water molecules (and other molecules like $CO_{2}$, $NH_{3}$) present in most materials readily absorb infrared waves.

Upon absorption, the thermal motion of these molecules increases, which causes the material to heat up.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) provides the correct physical explanation for why they are called heat waves.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A plane electromagnetic wave with a magnetic field amplitude of $2 \times 10^{-7} \text{ T}$ falls normally on a non-reflecting surface of area $2\pi \text{ m}^2$. The total energy delivered to the surface in $1 \text{ minute}$ is:

(Take $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \text{ T m A}^{-1}$)
questions.solution:
The intensity $I$ of an electromagnetic wave in terms of its magnetic field amplitude $B_0$ is given by:

$I = \dfrac{B_0^2 c}{2\mu_0}$

Substitute the given values:
$I = \dfrac{(2 \times 10^{-7})^2 \times (3 \times 10^8)}{2 \times (4\pi \times 10^{-7})}$

$I = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-14} \times 3 \times 10^8}{8\pi \times 10^{-7}}$

$I = \dfrac{12 \times 10^{-6}}{8\pi \times 10^{-7}} = \dfrac{120}{8\pi} = \dfrac{15}{\pi} \text{ W m}^{-2}$

The total energy $E$ delivered to the surface is:
$E = I \times A \times t$

Given the area $A = 2\pi \text{ m}^2$ and time $t = 1 \text{ minute} = 60 \text{ s}$:
$E = \left(\dfrac{15}{\pi}\right) \times (2\pi) \times 60$

$E = 30 \times 60 = 1800 \text{ J}$

Answer: $1800 \text{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Assertion (A): For an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum along the negative z-axis, if the electric field is along the positive x-axis, then the magnetic field must be along the positive y-axis.

Reason (R): The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the vector $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$, and the electric and magnetic fields are mutually perpendicular.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave is given by the cross product of the electric and magnetic field vectors, i.e., $\vec{v} \parallel \vec{E} \times \vec{B}$.

Given that the wave propagates along the negative z-axis, the direction of propagation is $-\hat{k}$.

The electric field is along the positive x-axis, so $\vec{E}$ is along $+\hat{i}$.

We need to find the direction of $\vec{B}$ such that $\hat{i} \times \vec{B} = -\hat{k}$.

Since $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, it follows that $\hat{i} \times (-\hat{j}) = -\hat{k}$.

Therefore, the magnetic field must be along the negative y-axis ($-\hat{j}$).

The Assertion states that the magnetic field is along the positive y-axis, which is incorrect. The Reason correctly states the principle for finding the propagation direction. Thus, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The electric field of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is given by the equation $E_x = 30 \sin(ky - \omega t) \text{ V/m}$. The average intensity of the electromagnetic wave is nearly:
(Take $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$ and $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \text{ C}^2/\text{N m}^2$)
questions.solution:
From the given equation, the amplitude of the electric field is $E_0 = 30 \text{ V/m}$.

The average intensity of an electromagnetic wave is given by the formula:
$I = \dfrac{1}{2} c \varepsilon_0 E_0^2$

Substituting the standard values:
$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (3 \times 10^8) \times (8.85 \times 10^{-12}) \times (30)^2$
$I = 1.5 \times 10^8 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 900$
$I = 1350 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-4}$
$I = 1.19475 \text{ W/m}^2 \approx 1.2 \text{ W/m}^2$

Note: Forgetting the factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ leads to the peak intensity ($2.4 \text{ W/m}^2$), which is a common error.

Answer: $1.2 \text{ W/m}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in a non-magnetic dielectric medium with a refractive index of $3$ is given by $\vec{E} = 60\pi \sin(kx - \omega t) \hat{j}$ V/m. The average intensity of the electromagnetic wave is:
questions.solution:
The amplitude of the electric field is $E_0 = 60\pi$ V/m.

The average intensity of an electromagnetic wave in a medium is given by $I = \dfrac{1}{2} \epsilon v E_0^2$, where $\epsilon$ is the permittivity of the medium and $v$ is the speed of the wave.

For a non-magnetic medium, the refractive index is $n = \sqrt{\epsilon_r}$, so $\epsilon = n^2 \epsilon_0$. The speed of the wave is $v = \dfrac{c}{n}$.

Substituting these into the intensity formula gives:
$I = \dfrac{1}{2} (n^2 \epsilon_0) \left(\dfrac{c}{n}\right) E_0^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} n \epsilon_0 c E_0^2$

We know that $\epsilon_0 c = \dfrac{1}{\mu_0 c} = \dfrac{1}{120\pi} \Omega^{-1}$.

Substituting the values $n = 3$ and $E_0 = 60\pi$ V/m:
$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times \dfrac{1}{120\pi} \times (60\pi)^2$

$I = \dfrac{3}{240\pi} \times 3600\pi^2 = 45\pi$ W/m$^2$.

Answer: $45\pi$ W/m$^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave propagating in vacuum, what fraction of the total average energy density is contributed by the electric field component? (where $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum)
questions.solution:
In an electromagnetic wave, the energy is equally divided between the electric and magnetic fields.

The average energy density of the electric field ($u_E$) is equal to the average energy density of the magnetic field ($u_B$).

Total average energy density, $u = u_E + u_B = 2u_E$

Therefore, the fraction of the total energy density contributed by the electric field is $\dfrac{u_E}{u} = \dfrac{u_E}{2u_E} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.q:
Arrange the following electromagnetic waves in the decreasing order of their wavelengths:

(A) X-rays
(B) Microwaves
(C) Ultraviolet rays
(D) Infrared rays

Choose the correct option:
questions.solution:
The electromagnetic spectrum, arranged in decreasing order of wavelength (or increasing order of frequency), is as follows:

Radio waves > Microwaves > Infrared > Visible light > Ultraviolet > X-rays > Gamma rays.

Comparing the given waves:
Microwaves (B) have the longest wavelength (approx. $10^{-2}\text{ m}$).
Infrared rays (D) have a shorter wavelength (approx. $10^{-4}\text{ m}$).
Ultraviolet rays (C) have an even shorter wavelength (approx. $10^{-8}\text{ m}$).
X-rays (A) have the shortest wavelength among the given options (approx. $10^{-10}\text{ m}$).

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of wavelengths is (B) > (D) > (C) > (A).

Answer: (B) > (D) > (C) > (A)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electromagnetic wave has a wavelength $\lambda_0$ in vacuum. It enters a material medium of relative permittivity $\epsilon_r$ and relative permeability $\mu_r$. The wavelength of the wave in this medium will be:
questions.solution:
When an electromagnetic wave travels from one medium to another, its frequency ($f$) remains constant.

The speed of the wave in vacuum is $c = f \lambda_0$, and in the medium it is $v = f \lambda$.

Therefore, the wavelength in the medium is directly proportional to the wave speed:
$\lambda = \lambda_0 \left(\dfrac{v}{c}\right)$

The speed of light in a medium is given by $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$.

Substituting this into the wavelength equation yields:
$\lambda = \lambda_0 \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}} \right) = \dfrac{\lambda_0}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\lambda_0}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave travelling in a lossless, non-magnetic dielectric medium (dielectric constant $\epsilon_r = 4$) is given by:
$B_z = 2 \times 10^{-8} \sin(1.5\pi \times 10^8 t + \pi x)$ T.

Match the wave parameters in List-I with their corresponding values in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Speed of the wave in the medium (in m/s)(I) $3$
(B) Wavelength of the wave (in m)(II) $+x$
(C) Amplitude of the electric field (in V/m)(III) $1.5 \times 10^8$
(D) Direction of propagation(IV) $2$
(V) $-x$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The speed of the wave in the medium is $v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_r}} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{4}} = 1.5 \times 10^8$ m/s. (Matches A-III)

From the given equation, the wave vector $k = \pi$ rad/m. The wavelength is $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi} = 2$ m. (Matches B-IV)

The amplitude of the electric field is $E_0 = vB_0 = (1.5 \times 10^8) \times (2 \times 10^{-8}) = 3$ V/m. (Matches C-I)

The phase of the wave is $(1.5\pi \times 10^8 t + \pi x)$. The positive sign between the time and space terms indicates that the wave is propagating in the $-x$ direction. (Matches D-V)

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(V).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(V)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Assume that a radio station is about $200 \mathrm{~km}$ away from your location and the station operates at $972 \mathrm{kHz}$. How long does it take for an electromagnetic signal to travel from the station to you and how many wave crests does it send out per second?

Time taken by wave to travel
$=\frac{200 \mathrm{~km}}{3 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}}=6.667 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~s} \approx 666 \mu \mathrm{s}$
Number of crests per second $=$ Frequency
Frequency $=972 \mathrm{kHz}=9.72 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~Hz}\therefore \quad$ There are $9.72 \times 10^5$ crests per second.

questions.solution:
The de-Broglie wavelength is given by
$\lambda=\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E}}$ ...(i)
where, $E$ is the energy of the electron. The cut-off wavelength $\lambda_0$ is given by
$\lambda_0=\frac{h C}{E}$ ...(ii)
From Eq. (i),
$\lambda^2=\frac{h^2}{2 m E}\Rightarrow \quad E=\frac{h^2}{2 m X^2}$ ... (iii)
Substituting the value of $E$ from Eq. (ii), we get
$\lambda_0=\frac{h c}{\frac{h^2}{2 m \lambda^2}}=\frac{2 m c \lambda^2}{h}$
